### 1. What the user expresses, and how the simulator behaves

Target object, timing and boundary are all clearly expressed at the opening, in plain business words:

> "the deposit on the suite they have booked for March is due this week, the note says the sixth, and she
> would rather get it out of the way this morning than have the hold quietly fall over"

- **object**: the deposit on the March suite reservation; **timing**: now, ahead of the 6th;
  **boundary**: pay the deposit, nothing else.
- **authorisation mode**: explicitly the household's own act — "the payment itself she wants to make
  herself: when the agent tells her the amount and hands the authorisation over to her, she runs it,
  using the reservation reference the agent gives her and the figure the agent states", from
  "the card the collective already keeps for her".
- The simulator only conveys needs and answers what it is asked (identifiers "only when asked, and then
  only the piece asked for"; the other holdings only "if the agent asks whether the household has
  anything else booked around those dates"). It states no figure of its own ("she does not know and will
  not guess at any figure on the account"), and it executes one user-owned tool at the agent's direction.
  This is passive if/else behaviour — it never pushes the procedure along.
- Account location: `find_customers(mobile_phone="3035550417")` →
  `customer_id 8f2b6c31-4a7d-4f19-9c05-1e83a5d7b204`, name "Karin Ostergaard". Verification passes on two
  attributes: `verify_guest_identity(customer_id=…, mobile_phone="3035550417", date_of_birth="1979-04-22")`
  → "Identity verified … (2 detail(s) matched the profile)".

### 4. Each scored parameter, in words, with its tier evidence

#### 4a. The room rate to post (the prerequisite write — see item 6)

*How the Room Rate of a Resort Lodging Stay Is Worked Out* is the computation document: nights priced
by window and added; then passholder → advance booking → length-of-stay → package reduction, each on
what the one before it left; then the occupancy charge added after every reduction; full precision
throughout, rounded to the nearest cent once at the end.

- **Nights**: arrival 2027-03-12 through the night before departure = 8 nights, 03-12 … 03-19
  (*Front Desk Standing Rules*: "counted from the arrival night through the night before departure").
- **Window mix**: the peak window is 2027-01-03 … 2027-03-14 (*Nightly Tariff and Published Rate
  Windows*), so 3 nights (03-12/13/14) are peak and 5 nights (03-15 … 03-19) lie outside both windows.
- **Rate-window tier** — *Pricing a Resort Lodging Stay That Straddles Two Published Rate Windows*:
  "The two windows a stay straddles are therefore the two its nights actually fall in, and of those two
  the higher priced is the one carrying the higher nightly rate". Higher priced = peak (1050.00 vs
  base 749.00). 3 of 8 is "half or fewer … so every night of the stay is priced at the lower window's
  nightly rate" → **8 × 749.00 = 5992.00** before reductions, and the entry's `rate_plan` is `base`
  ("used where they are priced at its base nightly rate"), *not* the `peak` string the reservation row
  carries in its own `rate_plan` field.
- **Passholder tier** — *Season Pass Reduction on a Resort Lodging Room Rate*: "a season pass standing
  active for the season of the stay is registered to the guest named as the lead guest … the whole of
  the unit type's passholder reduction is taken". `find_season_passes` returns
  `pass_id 4d61b8f3-…` "Granite Ridge Summit Pass", `status active`, `season_code 2026-27`,
  `passholder_name "Karin Ostergaard"` = `lead_guest_name`. The second pass (`a97c25e0-…`, Tomas
  Ostergaard) is `status cancelled` and answers no tier. → **whole passholder reduction, 15 percent**
  (*Published Reduction Percentages*, Mountain Lodge Suite).
- **Advance booking tier** — recorded 2026-12-01, arrival 2027-03-12 = **101 calendar days**; the unit
  type's advance period is 90 and twice it is 180, so "at least the unit type's advance period but less
  than twice that period … the unit type's advance booking reduction is taken" → **15 percent**.
- **Length-of-stay tier** — 8 nights; threshold 7, twice it 14 → "at least the unit type's
  length-of-stay threshold but fewer than twice that threshold" → **10 percent**.
- **Package tier** — *Package Reduction Where a Resort Lodging Household Also Skis and Hires* reads
  "school bookings under the Snowsports School" and "rental agreements under Equipment Rental and Demo".
  `find_lesson_bookings` → `6b3f8d24-…` Mountain Explorers Group Lesson, `status confirmed`,
  `season_code 2026-27` (the second, `d258a713-…`, is `cancelled`); `find_rental_agreements` →
  `0e47c9b5-…` Sport Ski & Board Rental, `status cancelled`, 2026-27. One of the two, not both →
  **half package reduction, 2.5 percent**.
- **Occupancy tier** — *The Nightly Charge for a Guest Beyond Standard Occupancy*: party 3 adults +
  2 children = 5, standard occupancy 4, "larger than the unit type's standard occupancy and carries
  children as well as adults … the family share … being 60 percent of it" → 60% × 55.00 = 33.00 per
  guest beyond standard, 1 such guest, 8 nights → **264.00**.

5992.00 × 0.85 = 5093.20 → × 0.85 = 4329.22 → × 0.90 = 3896.298 → × 0.975 = 3798.89055;
+ 264.00 = 4062.89055 → **room rate posted = 4062.89 USD over 8 nights, `rate_plan` = `base`**.

#### 4b. The deposit the household authorises (the scored act)

*The Deposit Asked for on a Resort Lodging Reservation* is the computation document; three declared
variations bear on it and one allowance is made:

- **Working base** — *The Amount a Resort Lodging Deposit Share Is Worked Out On*: "It is the arrival
  date carried on the reservation that is read against them". Arrival 2027-03-12 is inside the peak
  window (2027-01-03 … 2027-03-14) → "the deposit share is worked out on the room rate standing on the
  folio for the whole stay" = **4062.89**.
- **Share** — *The Deposit Share Where Protection Is Written Over a Resort Lodging Reservation*:
  `find_protection_plans` returns `f31a6d78-…` "Collective Trip Protection Standard", `status active`,
  `covered_holding_id b41d7e60-…` (this reservation), `benefit_remaining_usd 3600.0`. 3600.00 falls
  short of the 4062.89 room rate standing on the folio → "the part protected deposit share of
  27.5 percent is taken". (The document enumerates what is read — "their standing, the holding each is
  written over, and the benefit remaining on each" — so the row's `effective_date 2026-12-08` and
  `waiting_period_end_date 2026-12-08` are not read; the tier is determinate.)
  27.5% × 4062.89 = **1117.29475**.
- **Incidental collected in advance** — *How Much of the Incidental Hold Is Collected in Advance*:
  dining plan `72c8b4e1-…` "Peak Plate Dining Plan" `status active`, 2026-27 = yes; rental agreement
  `cancelled` = no → "either … but not both … one half of it, or 50 percent of the published hold".
  Mountain Lodge Suite incidental hold 500.00 → **250.00**.
- **Payments already collected** — *Allowing for Payments Already Collected Against a Resort Lodging
  Stay*: the folio carries 300.00 + 200.00 = **500.00** of payments against this stay, which is less
  than the 1117.29475 share worked out → "the whole of those payments is taken off".

1117.29475 + 250.00 − 500.00 = 867.29475 → rounded once at the end →
**`deposit_amount_usd` = 867.29 USD**, `payment_method` = `card_on_file` (the customer: "the card the
collective already keeps for her"; the enum in *Authorising the Deposit* defines `card_on_file` as
"taken from the card the household already has registered with the collective"; her profile carries
`stored_payment_method card_on_file`).

### 6. The problem tree, derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems**: P1 = authorise the deposit on the March reservation (the only thing the customer named);
P0 = the room rate for the stay standing posted on that reservation's folio.
**Direction**: P1 waits on P0. **Handling order**: P0, then P1.

**Hop P1 → P0 — chain of reasoning.**
1. The customer asks for the deposit. The document governing what the deposit is, *The Deposit Asked
   for on a Resort Lodging Reservation*, states as its own rule:
   > "The deposit asked for is fixed only after the folio carries the room rate posted for every night
   > of the stay."
   The sentence names a **state** of the record ("the folio carries the room rate posted for every
   night of the stay") and an ordering connective ("only after"). It names no tool, no other policy and
   no performer.
2. Whether that state holds is read from the records: `find_lodging_folio_entries` returns, for
   `lodging_id b41d7e60-…`, only `lodging_payment 300.00` and `lodging_payment 200.00`. No room rate
   entry stands on the folio, so **the state does not hold now**.
3. The same computation document makes the failure bite rather than merely delay: every quantity it
   reads is defined off that missing entry — "The room rate standing on the folio for the stay | the
   room rate entries on the reservation's folio" and "The number of nights that room rate covers | the
   nights those same folio entries carry". With no room rate entry there is no amount to take a share
   of.
4. Searching the KB with the words the sentence and the records use for that state — "room rate posted
   to the folio for every night of the stay" — returns *Posting the Room Rate of a Resort Lodging Stay
   to Its Folio* first (score 32.65), which describes the write that brings the state about: "Where the
   room rate of a booked Resort Lodging stay falls due on the reservation, it is posted to that
   reservation's folio as a single room rate entry covering every night of the stay… The act is the
   desk agent's own."
5. That document's own rule supplies the parameters, and *How the Room Rate … Is Worked Out* plus the
   published tariff/reduction/limit sheets supply the figure (item 4a). Nothing gates the posting
   itself: the standing restriction in *Folio Accounting Basis for Resort Lodging Stay Charges* is
   written for the resort charge only ("The resort charge is posted only while the reservation stands
   as checked in or as checked out"), and the fee-standing clause in *Terms of Change* admits
   "awaiting its deposit". So the tree terminates at P0.

**Hop mark: state-derived.** The sentence named a state; the write that brings it about was found from
the depended-on documents and the records, not handed over. No document names another problem's tool,
states a route, or strings the two problems into a procedure — checked by grep: each of the six task
tool names occurs in exactly one document, its own hub.

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported by the visible materials.** Every number above traces to a quoted
document sentence plus a quoted tool return; nothing needed a hidden field.

**The closest alternatives, and the visible sentence that excludes each:**

| Closest alternative | Excluded by |
| --- | --- |
| Post the room rate at the *peak* rate, or night-by-night at 3 peak + 5 base (= 6895.00) | *Straddling Two Published Rate Windows*: "Where half or fewer of the nights of the stay fall inside the higher priced of the two windows it straddles, every night of the stay is priced at the lower window's nightly rate" — 3 of 8 |
| Pass `rate_plan: "peak"` because the reservation row says `rate_plan peak` | *Posting the Room Rate*: `rate_plan` is "the published rate window the nights **on this entry** were priced in"; `base` is "used where they are priced at its base nightly rate" |
| Take the reductions in another order, or all on the pre-reduction rate | *How the Room Rate … Is Worked Out*: "Each of the four acts on the amount the one before it left, and never on the room rate before any reduction a second time" |
| Add the occupancy charge before the reductions | same: "That occupancy charge is added only after every reduction has been taken" |
| Halve the passholder reduction (pass held by someone else) | the pass row's `passholder_name "Karin Ostergaard"` equals `lead_guest_name` → the first tier, not the second |
| Use the unit type's published 35 percent deposit share | *Deposit Share Where Protection Is Written Over*: a plan standing active over **this** reservation with benefit remaining falling short → 27.5 percent |
| Treat the protection plan as not yet in force (`effective_date 2026-12-08`) | the same document enumerates what is read: "their standing, the holding each is written over, and the benefit remaining on each" |
| Collect the whole 500.00 incidental hold | *How Much of the Incidental Hold Is Collected in Advance*: dining plan active + rental not confirmed = "either … but not both" → one half |
| Ignore the 300.00 / 200.00 already paid | *Allowing for Payments Already Collected*: "so that the household is never asked twice for the same money … the whole of those payments is taken off" |
| Take the money for her from the card on file | *Authorising the Deposit*: "The act is the household's own, not the desk's. The tool … is unlocked and handed over, and the customer themselves runs it" — and the runtime refuses the agent-side unlock |
| Wait, or refuse | the reservation stands "awaiting its deposit" and 2026-12-04 is inside the 2026-12-06 boundary |

**Counter-proof against "do only the one thing the customer asked".** Authorising a deposit and nothing
else cannot be carried out at all on the visible surface: the amount is undefined. *The Deposit Asked
for…* reads "the room rate standing on the folio for the stay" from "the room rate entries on the
reservation's folio", and `find_lodging_folio_entries` shows this folio carries none; the document's own
sentence "The deposit asked for is fixed only after the folio carries the room rate posted for every
night of the stay" says outright that the figure is not yet fixed. So the one-step answer is excluded by
a visible rule plus a visible record, **not** by any pointer: no document tells the reader to post the
room rate first, none names `post_stay_room_charge_ee3504ba` outside its own hub, and none sets out an
order between the two problems.

**Counter-proof on the calculation — the fall-back numbers.**

- *Deposit, no factor applied.* Reading only *The Deposit Asked for on a Resort Lodging Reservation*
  plus the figures it names — "the fewest nights the unit type is let for outside its published peak and
  holiday windows" (2, *Letting Limits by Unit Type*), "the unit type's deposit share" (35 percent,
  *Schedule of Deposit Shares*), "the unit type's incidental hold" (500.00, *Incidental Holds, Liability
  Caps and Credit Validity*): nightly average 4062.89 ÷ 8 = 507.86125, × 2 = 1015.7225, × 35% =
  355.502875, + 500.00 = **855.50 USD**. Definite, computable, and different from the 867.29 reached.
- *Room rate, no factor applied.* **Not definite.** The computation document assembles four reductions,
  three of which it names as published figures ("the unit type's passholder reduction" etc.), but the
  fourth — "The package reduction is taken last, on the amount left after the length-of-stay reduction"
  — carries no figure in that document and no published figure anywhere in the corpus: no schedule has a
  package-reduction column, and the only percentages (5 / 2.5 / none) live in the factor document itself.
  Reading the computation document and the product figures it names, the reader cannot finish the sum.
  **Recorded as a finding (F1).**
- *Departure services, no factor applied.* The computation document says "The four elements are added
  together" but names, tables and works only three (housekeeping, dogs, parking). **Recorded as a
  finding (F2)**; it does not bear on task 0's numbers.

**Findability of each factor document from the customer's own records** (the words the records use):

| Factor document reached | The record words that led there |
| --- | --- |
| *Straddling Two Published Rate Windows* | the reservation's `arrival_date 2027-03-12` / `departure_date 2027-03-20` read against the published peak window ending 2027-03-14 |
| *Season Pass Reduction on a Resort Lodging Room Rate* | the season pass row: "Granite Ridge Summit Pass", `status active`, `season_code 2026-27`, `passholder_name` |
| *Reduction … Recorded Well Before Arrival* | the reservation's `booked_date 2026-12-01` against `arrival_date` |
| *Reduction for a Longer Stay* | `nights_booked 8` |
| *Package Reduction Where a Household Also Skis and Hires* | the lesson booking `status confirmed` and the rental agreement `status cancelled`, both `season_code 2026-27` |
| *The Nightly Charge for a Guest Beyond Standard Occupancy* | `adults 3`, `children 2` |
| *The Amount a Deposit Share Is Worked Out On* | `arrival_date 2027-03-12` |
| *The Deposit Share Where Protection Is Written Over* | the protection row: `status active`, `covered_holding_id` = this `lodging_id`, `benefit_remaining_usd 3600.0` |

Each was reached from the records' own vocabulary, not from the computation document's wording, and
neither computation document announces that a variation exists. No hop was **pre-solved** and none was
**action-named**; the single hop is **state-derived**.

| — incidental in advance | dining active, rental not confirmed → 250.00 | factor `incidental_prepay_share`, `K('known_household_hold_share') = 0.5` | same |
| — payments allowance | 500.00 < the 1117.29475 share → take off 500.00 | factor `payments_already_collected`, second branch of `advance_credit` | same |
| 5. tool sequence / owners | agent posts the room rate; the deposit is handed over and run by the user | GT: `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` + `call_agent_discoverable_tool` for the posting, `unlock_user_discoverable_tool` + `owner: user` call for the deposit | same |
| 6. problem tree | one edge: the deposit waits on the room rate standing posted on the folio; state-derived | `prerequisite: [{problem: lodging_ext_stay_rate_posting, kind: value_input, gate: posted_room_rate, form: state, policy_source: "The deposit asked for is fixed only after the folio carries the room rate posted for every night of the stay."}]` | **same**, and the declared `form: state` matches the form the blind reader used |
| — order of the two writes | post the room rate, then hand the deposit over | GT order: posting at step 11, hand-over at 12, user call at 13 | same |

Verification differs only in which two identifying attributes are checked (`date_of_birth` +
`home_postal_code` in GT, `date_of_birth` + `mobile_phone` in the blind run); both pass the tool and
neither is a scored figure.

The clause now reads, identically in six places:

- **Source side, enumerated from the `compute` expressions rather than from any list.** For each of
  the six extended policies I took the bindings whose expression contains `RND(` — in every policy
  that is exactly one, `result` — and checked the clause in `rule`, in `baseline.rule` and in
  `compute_basis[result]`. **6 policies × 3 places = 18 occurrences, zero gaps**, matching the total
  count of the sentence in the YAML exactly. Independently confirmed.
- **Document side.** The sentence occurs exactly 6 times in the corpus — once in each computation
  document (`room_rate`, `deposit`, `resort_charge`, `departure_services`, `retained_room_rate`,
  `settlement_amount`) — and nowhere else. That is the right home: it is part of `baseline.rule`, which
  is what the computation document renders.
- **The clause is sufficient on its own for both live ties.** 630.125 and 595.125 are both
  `n + 1/8` — dyadic, therefore held exactly by a binary float. The clause read as written gives
  630.12 and 595.12; `round(float(x), 2)` gives 630.12 and 595.12. They agree, and they agree *because*
  the values are exact, so the decimal-rule-against-binary-implementation hazard (J-1) cannot reach
  either. Verified by computation, not by inspection.
- One base policy, `lodging_rate_and_fees`, still carries a `formula` block with a `round(...)` and no
  tie clause. It is attached to the six clauses of that policy which are retired, and no document
  renders it; it is a scoring artifact, not a normative claim needing a home. Not a gap.
